Photograph: Katherine Delgado/AP US immigration Father of USS Lincoln sailor taken into ICE detention while son deployed in Middle East Joshua Aviles says he is on a nine-month Middle East deployment and learned his has father has been arrested while he was waiting for green card approval Reuters Mon 24 Aug 2026 01.42 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google The father of a US sailor on board the USS Abraham Lincoln ⁠aircraft carrier deployed in the Middle East during the Iran war has been taken into federal immigration detention, the sailor ⁠said. The border ​patrol arrested Luis Manuel Aviles Roa, originally from Nicaragua, after conducting a vehicle stop in Key West, Florida, a spokesperson for the US homeland security department said on Sunday. Joshua Aviles, the son, posted: “I’ve been deployed for over nine months, out ⁠at sea in the Middle East aboard the USS Abraham Lincoln, fighting for a country ​that has given me everything. ICE agent jailed on allegations of breaking into ex-girlfriend’s apartment Read more “I just got a call that my dad ‌was taken by ICE.” His father had his driver’s licence, social security card and work permit, Aviles said. “We have done everything through immigration to get his green card approved, and we are just waiting. This is heartbreaking for me. I don’t know how I can mentally continue working 12+ hour days ‌knowing that my dad is somewhere, possibly being treated like a criminal.” The DHS said Luis Manuel Aviles Roa ​entered the US illegally and would remain in immigration and customs enforcement detention pending removal proceedings. “Having a family member in the military is not a free pass to violate our nation’s laws,” the DHS said. Rights groups say the immigration crackdown under Donald Trump has violated free ​speech and due process ​rights and created an unsafe environment, ​particularly for ethnic minorities, who have raised concerns about racial profiling. The ​Lincoln, which left ‌the Middle East ​on Saturday, did ​not make a port call in more than 200 days. That set a modern-day record for consecutive days at sea, according to Democratic lawmakers who called for answers after sailors’ families raised concerns about about poor living conditions and morale on board. The USS George Washington aircraft carrier arrived in the Middle East last week , where it is expected to relieve the USS Abraham Lincoln. https://www.politico.eu/article/zack-pol.text: LONDON — Zack Polanski’s bid for a Westminster seat ended in defeat Friday as Labour held Holborn and St Pancras in a by-election. Labour’s Sagal Abdi-Wali took the central London House of Commons seat with 12,292 votes. Green Leader Polanski came in second with 8,928. The vote was triggered after Keir Starmer stood down as an MP last month after being ousted as U.K. prime minister. Advertisement Advertisement It is a symbolic early boost for Starmer’s replacement, Andy Burnham, who has shifted the ruling Labour Party to the left since taking charge, and toughened the U.K.’s stance on Israel by announcing plans to sanction West Bank settlements last month. The north London seat has been held by Labour since its creation in 1983 — but it is a disappointing result for the left-wing Green Party, which poured significant resources into getting its high-profile leader elected. The Greens took 33% of the vote to Labour’s 45% on a turnout of 38.8%. Moments after the declaration Polanski said he would stay on as party leader. “I’ve taken a loss tonight, but our movement is so much bigger than one election or one motion,” he said. U.K. polling expert John Curtice said the Holborn and St Pancras result is “still by far and away [the Greens’] second best ever result in a parliamentary by-election.” But he warned the Greens are “now operating in a more politically competitive environment.” Advertisement Advertisement “The trouble is that when you manage to bring down an unpopular leader of your opponents, you’ve then got to deal with the consequences, which is in this case is that Labour have put in place somebody who is more popular,” Curtice said of the Greens’ boast that their success earlier this year helped oust Starmer. Polanski’s defeat also comes as Green Party divisions are spilling into the open after members passed a controversial motion declaring Zionism to be a form of racism at their party conference last weekend. One London councillor said the move had been “electoral suicide,” and shortly after polls closed Thursday the veteran former MP Caroline Lucas told the BBC that Polanski, who did not attend the vote in Brighton, “should have been” and should now “show the leadership that was frankly missing on Sunday.” Asked if Polanski should stand down, the former party leader, who was the first Green MP to be elected to the House of Commons, said: “I think let’s just see what happens in the coming days and weeks.” This developing story is being updated.
